content:
Hi Trevor.

Move the email from outbox to draft. From there you can try and send them again.

Emails that remain in the outbox after a period of time have likely been marked as permanent send failures. Once marked, the app will never try and send them again.

TBA marks emails permanent send failures under the following circumstances.

1. A temporary send failure was experiences. Poor network signal and server side issues being two examples. The app retries sending the email 5 more times, then marks it a permanent send failure.

2. The size of your email was greater than the maximum size your mail provider allows. TBA checks this size before attempting to send. If it's too big, it's marked as a permanent send failure.

The app provides a silent notification in the notification shade when emails are marked as such.

See below for more info. https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-android/issues/4602

content:
Sounds like you overloaded the "fetch more" " queue Try, in order:

Give it 10-15 min on strong wifi — it may just be grinding through the backlog silently. Clear app cache: Android Settings → Apps → Thunderbird → Storage → Clear Cache (keeps your account, dumps the stuck sync). Force stop → reopen the app. Lower the sync limit: folder settings → "messages to keep synced" → smaller number (e.g. 25). Remove and re-add the account — since it's IMAP and your real email is untouched, this is zero-risk and guarantees a clean fetch.

Since you rarely use the phone for email anyway, I'd skip straight to clearing the cache, and if that doesn't work in a minute or two, just remove/re-add the account.

content:
It looks like you're using incorrect server names in the TB config.

According to dreamhost's own documentation at: https://help.dreamhost.com/hc/en-us/articles/214918038-Email-client-configuration-overview

Incoming server: POP: hostname = pop.dreamhost.com, port = 995, Security = SSL/TSL IMAP: hostname = imap.dreamhost.com, port = 993, Security = SSL/TLS Outgoing server: SMTP: hostname = smtp.dreamhost.com, port = 587, Security = StartTLS

Those match the certificate. You should use these instead.

Dreamhost's own documentation also state this as the resolution for the certificate error. https://help.dreamhost.com/hc/en-us/articles/215306748-Certificate-domain-mismatch-error-when-connecting-to-a-DreamHost-mail-server

You should also be aware of the difference between pop and Imap. Pop is designed for use on a single device. I'd recommend you use Imap in the TB mobile app.
